facts.raw_span: progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction
a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
A hypervascular and pulsatile tumor occupies almost the entire right nasal fossa
Enhanced CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
Confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
The sinonasal tumor had low uptake, indicative of thyroid tissue with low iodine avidity
Serum Thyroglobulin: 4432 ng/mL (significantly elevated)
Costal Biopsy: Pointed to VTC metastasis
Sinonasal Tumor Biopsy: Confirmed VTC metastasis

concepts.why: The presence of a hypervascular and pulsatile tumor in the nasal cavity, along with elevated serum thyroglobulin levels and biopsy results confirming VTC metastasis, supports this diagnosis.
The endoscopic examination and imaging studies reveal a voluminous, pulsatile, and highly vascularized mass in the nasal cavity, indicating a tumor.
The presence of thyroid tissue with low iodine avidity in the nasal cavity, along with metastasis in the rib and vertebral lesions, supports this diagnosis.
The endoscopic examination and imaging studies reveal a hypervascular and pulsatile tumor in the nasal cavity, indicating a vascular origin.
The presence of metastasis in multiple locations, including the rib and vertebral lesions, supports this diagnosis.
The endoscopic examination and imaging studies reveal a hypervascular and pulsatile mass in the nasal cavity, indicating a possible vascular malformation.
The patient presents with progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction, indicating a possible tumor or other mass in the nasal cavity.

rationales.F01: Nasal obstruction is a common symptom of various conditions, including vascular tumors and nasal cavity tumors.
rationales.F02: The presence of a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities is highly suggestive of a vascular tumor.
rationales.F04: The presence of a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra is highly suggestive of a metastatic disease.
rationales.F08: Elevated serum thyroglobulin levels are indicative of thyroid tissue, which is consistent with thyroid cancer or metastasis.
rationales.F10: The biopsy results confirming VTC metastasis provide strong evidence for a vascular tumor with metastasis.
